library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gaurav_2026_favezelimab"))$reference`
* Description (PK): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gaurav_2026_favezelimab"))$description`
* Description (ORR): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Gaurav_2026_favezelimab_orr"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70658> (open access, PMC13330136)

Gaurav 2026 reports two models, packaged as two files:

* `Gaurav_2026_favezelimab` -- the population PK model: two compartments with
  parallel linear and Michaelis-Menten (target-mediated) elimination, a
  full-model covariate structure on CL and Vc, and time-varying anti-drug
  antibody (ADA) status on the linear component of CL.
* `Gaurav_2026_favezelimab_orr` -- the exposure-efficacy logistic regression
  of objective response rate (ORR) on the average favezelimab AUC in the
  phase 1 gastric cancer cohort.

The two exposure-safety analyses (Grade >= 3 drug-related adverse events and
drug-related adverse events of special interest) found no significant
exposure-response relationship, and the paper states that no further
modelling was done for them, so there is no model to package.

# Population

The PK analysis pooled 724 patients and 8980 serum concentrations from two
studies (Results, 'Patient Characteristics'; Supplementary Tables S1-S2):
the first-in-human phase 1 study MK-4280-001 (P001, n = 475; 7-800 mg IV Q3W
as monotherapy or with pembrolizumab, with or without chemotherapy or
lenvatinib) and the phase 3 KEYFORM-007 study (n = 249; favezelimab 800 mg
co-formulated with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W in PD-L1-positive previously
treated metastatic colorectal cancer). Median age was 59 years (25-85),
median weight 70.9 kg (33.0-145.9), 38.1% were female, 68.2% Caucasian and
27.1% Asian. Median albumin was 40 g/L; 51.9% had ECOG performance status 1;
29.8% had hepatic and 39.6% renal impairment of any degree. Overall 28.9% of
patients were ADA-positive at some point (26.2% at 800 mg), with a median
onset of about 3 weeks (Table S3).

The exposure-efficacy analysis used the 80 gastric cancer patients of P001
randomised to favezelimab 200 mg (n = 40) or 700 mg (n = 40) Q3W, each with
pembrolizumab 200 mg; 9 (11.3%) responded (Table S6).

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Gaurav_2026_favezelimab")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. Collected:

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` | log(0.0195 L/h) | Table 1, CL |
| `lvc` | log(3.08 L) | Table 1, Vc |
| `lq` | log(0.0322 L/h) | Table 1, Q |
| `lvp` | log(1.22 L) | Table 1, Vp |
| `lvmax` | log(13.6 ug/h) | Table 1, Vmax |
| `lkm` | log(49.5 ug/L) | Table 1, Km (unit: see Assumptions) |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.599, 0.353 | Table 1, body weight effects; reference 71 kg from the footnote equations |
| `e_alb_cl`, `e_alb_vc` | -1.11, -0.116 | Table 1, albumin effects; reference 40 g/L from the footnote equation |
| `e_age_cl` | -0.115 | Table 1, age effect on CL; reference 59 years = median (Table S2) |
| `e_male_cl`, `e_male_vc` | 0.200, 0.255 | Table 1, sex effects; applied to males per the footnote equations |
| `e_race_asian_cl`, `e_race_asian_vc` | -0.245, -0.0974 | Table 1, Asian race effects |
| `e_ecog_ge1_cl`, `e_ecog_ge1_vc` | 0.0742, -0.0031 | Table 1, ECOG effects |
| `e_hepimp_cl`, `e_hepimp_vc` | 0.0461, 0.0123 | Table 1, hepatic impairment effects |
| `e_renalimp_cl`, `e_renalimp_vc` | -0.0926, -0.0184 | Table 1, renal impairment effects |
| `e_ada_pos_cl` | 1.11 | Table 1, ADA effect on CL (functional form: see Assumptions) |
| `etalcl + etalvc` | var 0.167281, cov 0.01821195, var 0.033856 | Table 1, omega_CL 0.409, omega_Vc 0.184 (SDs), corr_Vc_CL 0.242 |
| `addSd` | 30.3 ng/mL | Table 1, additive error; unit from the Results text |
| `propSd` | 0.322 | Table 1, proportional error |
| Power / exponential covariate forms | n/a | Table 1 footnote |
| `d/dt(central)` with `vmax * Cc / (km + Cc)` | n/a | Results: '2-compartment TMDD model with MM approximation' |
| `logit_ref` | -2.48928 | Table S7, intercept |
| `e_auc_favezelimab_logit` | 4.36e-8 per ng*h/mL | Table S7, centred average AUC |
| `auc_favezelimab_ref` | 1.54e7 ng*h/mL | Digitised from Figure 3 (not printed) |

# Typical-value checks against the text

The Results give the typical CL and Vc 'for a male (non-Asian) weighing
71 kg, with an albumin level of 40 g/dL [sic; g/L], an ECOG status of zero,
and normal renal function' as 0.023 L/h and 3.94 L.

```{r typical-values}
ref_male <- data.frame(
  WT = 71, ALB = 40, AGE = 59, SEXF = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0, ECOG_GE1 = 0,
  HEPIMP = 0, RENALIMP = 0, ADA_POS = 0
)
cl_male <- 0.0195 * exp(0.200)
vc_male <- 3.08 * exp(0.255)
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Parameter = c("CL (L/h)", "Vc (L)"),
    Model = signif(c(cl_male, vc_male), 3),
    Published = c(0.023, 3.94)
  ),
  caption = "Typical male CL and Vc implied by Table 1 versus the Results text."
)
stopifnot(
  abs(cl_male / 0.023 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(vc_male / 3.94 - 1) < 0.02
)
```

Both agree within rounding (CL 0.0238 printed as 0.023; Vc 3.98 versus
3.94, a 1% difference). This is also what fixes the direction of the sex
effect: the 0.200 and 0.255 coefficients raise CL and Vc for MALES, so female
is the typical-value category of Table 1.

# Nonlinearity and the Km unit

The Methods give Km in ug/mL, Table 1 and the Results in ug/L. With
Km = 49.5 ug/L (= 49.5 ng/mL) the low-concentration Michaelis-Menten
clearance is Vmax / Km = 0.27 L/h, about twelve times the linear CL, which
produces the dose nonlinearity the paper describes ('PK exposure increased
with increase in dose and exhibited nonlinear PK at lower doses'). With
ug/mL the same arm would be 1000-fold weaker and the PK would be linear at
every studied dose. The dose-normalised cycle 1 AUC of a typical patient:

```{r km-check}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Gaurav_2026_favezelimab")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk)

# Typical-value solves of several subjects warn that the simulation has no
# omega; that is intended, so only that warning is muffled.
solve_typ <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(..., returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

typ_events <- function(dose, id, n_cyc = 1, ada_from = Inf, cov = ref_male) {
  obs_t <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_cyc) - 1, function(k) {
    k * 504 + c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, 72, 96, seq(120, 504, by = 24))
  }))
  obs_t <- sort(unique(obs_t))
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = (seq_len(n_cyc) - 1) * 504, evid = 1L, amt = dose,
    rate = dose / 0.5, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs <- data.frame(id = id, time = obs_t, evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  ev <- cbind(ev, cov[rep(1, nrow(ev)), setdiff(names(cov), "ADA_POS"), drop = FALSE])
  ev$ADA_POS <- as.integer(ev$time >= ada_from)
  ev
}

doses_mg <- c(7, 21, 70, 200, 700, 800)
ev_km <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses_mg), function(i) typ_events(doses_mg[i], id = i)))
ev_km$dose_mg <- doses_mg[ev_km$id]
sim_km <- solve_typ(mod_typ, ev_km, keep = "dose_mg")

nca_km_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  sim_km |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dose_mg),
  Cc ~ time | dose_mg + id
)
nca_km_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  ev_km |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_mg),
  amt ~ time | dose_mg + id
)
nca_km <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  nca_km_conc, nca_km_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 504, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
))
dn <- as.data.frame(nca_km) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::transmute(dose_mg, dnAUC = PPORRES / dose_mg)
dn |>
  dplyr::mutate(dnAUC = round(dnAUC), `Relative to 800 mg` = round(dnAUC / dnAUC[dose_mg == 800], 2)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg)" = dose_mg, "AUC0-21d / dose (ng*h/mL per mg)" = dnAUC) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Dose-normalised cycle 1 AUC, typical male patient.")
stopifnot(
  # TMDD makes the lowest dose clearly less than dose-proportional ...
  dn$dnAUC[dn$dose_mg == 7] / dn$dnAUC[dn$dose_mg == 800] < 0.75,
  # ... and the arm is saturated across the clinical range 200-800 mg.
  abs(dn$dnAUC[dn$dose_mg == 200] / dn$dnAUC[dn$dose_mg == 800] - 1) < 0.1
)
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation (800 mg Q3W)

No individual data are available. The virtual cohort below draws covariates
independently from the Table S2 marginal summaries: weight log-normal
(median 70.9 kg, SD about 18 kg, truncated to 33-146 kg), albumin normal
(mean 39.4 g/L, SD 5.1, truncated to 21-70.6), age normal (mean 58.6, SD
11.2, truncated to 25-85), 38.1% female, 27.1% Asian, 51.9% ECOG 1, 29.8%
hepatic impairment and 39.6% renal impairment. 26.2% of patients become
ADA-positive at 504 h (the Table S3 median onset at 800 mg is 502 h) and stay
positive, mirroring the source's last-observation-carried-forward handling.
Five cycles are simulated, as in the source's forest-plot simulations. The
infusion duration is not reported; 30 minutes is assumed.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261113)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261113)

rtrunc <- function(n, draw, lo, hi) {
  x <- draw(n)
  bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  while (any(bad)) {
    x[bad] <- draw(sum(bad))
    bad <- x < lo | x > hi
  }
  x
}

make_cohort <- function(n, dose, ada_pct, n_cyc, id_offset = 0L, treatment) {
  subj <- data.frame(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    WT = rtrunc(n, function(k) exp(rnorm(k, log(70.9), 0.242)), 33, 146),
    ALB = rtrunc(n, function(k) rnorm(k, 39.4, 5.12), 21, 70.6),
    AGE = rtrunc(n, function(k) rnorm(k, 58.6, 11.2), 25, 85),
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, 0.381),
    RACE_ASIAN = rbinom(n, 1, 0.271),
    ECOG_GE1 = rbinom(n, 1, 0.519),
    HEPIMP = rbinom(n, 1, 0.298),
    RENALIMP = rbinom(n, 1, 0.396),
    ADA_EVER = rbinom(n, 1, ada_pct)
  )
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
    typ_events(
      dose, id = subj$id[i], n_cyc = n_cyc,
      ada_from = if (subj$ADA_EVER[i] == 1) 504 else Inf,
      cov = subj[i, c("WT", "ALB", "AGE", "SEXF", "RACE_ASIAN", "ECOG_GE1", "HEPIMP", "RENALIMP")]
    )
  }))
  ev$treatment <- treatment
  ev$ADA_EVER <- subj$ADA_EVER[match(ev$id, subj$id)]
  ev
}

ev800 <- make_cohort(200, 800, 0.262, n_cyc = 5, treatment = "800 mg Q3W")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev800[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim800 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod_pk, ev800,
  keep = c("treatment", "ADA_EVER", "SEXF", "RACE_ASIAN", "ECOG_GE1", "HEPIMP", "RENALIMP", "WT", "ALB", "AGE"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

## Concentration-time profile (compare Figure 2)

Figure 2 of the paper is a prediction-corrected VPC pooled over all doses and
cycles against time after the previous dose. It cannot be reproduced exactly
without the data, but its observed medians, read off the figure by the
maintainers (5.4e4, 2.25e4, 1.13e4 and 6.0e3 ng/mL at 168, 336, 504 and
700 h), give a scale check for the dominant 800 mg regimen. The simulated
cycle 1 percentiles at 800 mg are plotted with those points. The simulated
800 mg medians sit 25-45% above the pooled observed medians, as expected when
Figure 2 also pools the lower-dose P001 cohorts.

```{r figure-2}
fig2_obs <- data.frame(time = c(168, 336, 504, 700), Cc = c(5.4e4, 2.25e4, 1.13e4, 6.0e3))

vpc800 <- sim800 |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 504) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q10 = quantile(Cc, 0.10), Q50 = median(Cc), Q90 = quantile(Cc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc800, aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = fig2_obs, aes(time, Cc), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(10, 1e7)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 24, 48, 72, 168, 336, 504, 672)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Favezelimab Cc (ng/mL)",
    title = "Cycle 1 at 800 mg: simulated median and 10th-90th percentiles",
    caption = "Crosses: observed medians digitised from Figure 2 of Gaurav 2026 (all doses, prediction-corrected)."
  )

chk2 <- vpc800 |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(168, 336, 504)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig2_obs, by = "time") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = Q50 / Cc)
knitr::kable(chk2 |> dplyr::select(time, Q50, Cc, ratio) |>
  dplyr::rename("Time (h)" = time, "Simulated median" = Q50, "Figure 2 median" = Cc, "Ratio" = ratio),
  digits = 2, caption = "Simulated cycle 1 median at 800 mg versus the Figure 2 observed median.")
# A mis-scaled volume, clearance or unit moves these medians by many-fold;
# the window allows for Figure 2 pooling doses, cycles and prediction correction.
stopifnot(all(chk2$ratio > 0.5 & chk2$ratio < 2))
```

## PKNCA: cycle 1 and steady state

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  sim800 |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment),
  Cc ~ time | treatment + id
)
nca_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  ev800 |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
nca800 <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  nca_conc, nca_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = c(0, 2016), end = c(504, 2520),
    cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cmin = c(FALSE, TRUE)
  )
))
nca800_df <- as.data.frame(nca800)
nca800_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(interval = ifelse(start == 0, "Cycle 1", "Cycle 5 (steady state)")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(interval, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::rename("Interval" = interval, "AUC0-21d (ng*h/mL)" = auclast, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA at 800 mg Q3W (n = 200).")
```

The paper prints no NCA values (the dose-normalised NCA of Figures S3-S4 is
graphical only), so there is no published table to compare against. At
saturating doses the steady-state AUC over a dosing interval should equal
dose / CL for each subject; the PKNCA result is checked against that below,
using each subject's individual CL in cycle 5.

```{r ss-auc-identity}
cl_c5 <- sim800 |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 2016, time <= 2520) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cl = mean(cl), .groups = "drop")
auc_c5 <- nca800_df |>
  dplyr::filter(start == 2016, PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(cl_c5, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = PPORRES / (800 / cl * 1000))
# The Michaelis-Menten arm and residual non-steady-state add a few percent.
stopifnot(abs(median(auc_c5$ratio) - 1) < 0.05)
```

## Covariate effects on steady-state AUC (compare Figure 1)

Figure 1 shows geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of AUC0-tau,ss by covariate
subgroup, from empirical Bayes estimates of the 800 mg patients. The
published subgroup GMRs include the effects of correlated covariates (for
example, females and Asians are lighter), whereas this virtual cohort draws
covariates independently, so the simulated GMRs isolate each model term and
are expected to be closer to 1 for sex and race. ECOG and hepatic
impairment, whose model terms are small, land near the published GMRs; the
renal-impairment GMR scatters around the model's exp(0.0926) = 1.10 because
of the 200-subject cohort.

```{r figure-1}
ss <- auc_c5 |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sim800 |> dplyr::distinct(id, ADA_EVER, SEXF, RACE_ASIAN, ECOG_GE1, HEPIMP, RENALIMP),
    by = "id"
  )
gmr <- function(x, g) exp(mean(log(x[g == 1])) - mean(log(x[g == 0])))
fig1 <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("ADA positive vs negative", "Asian vs Caucasian/other", "Female vs male",
                 "ECOG 1 vs 0", "Hepatic impaired vs normal", "Renal impaired vs normal"),
  Simulated = c(
    gmr(ss$PPORRES, ss$ADA_EVER), gmr(ss$PPORRES, ss$RACE_ASIAN), gmr(ss$PPORRES, ss$SEXF),
    gmr(ss$PPORRES, ss$ECOG_GE1), gmr(ss$PPORRES, ss$HEPIMP), gmr(ss$PPORRES, ss$RENALIMP)
  ),
  Published = c(0.807, 1.41, 1.39, 0.788, 0.88, 1.05)
)
knitr::kable(fig1, digits = 2, caption = "AUC0-tau,ss GMRs: simulated cohort versus Figure 1 of Gaurav 2026.")
```

The ADA effect deserves a closer look because its functional form is not
printed. Table 1 gives 'ADA Effect on CL' = 1.11. Read as a multiplicative
factor on linear CL, a typical patient who turns ADA-positive at the start of
cycle 2 has a steady-state AUC ratio of about 0.90; read as an exponential
coefficient, exp(1.11) = 3.03, the ratio would be about 0.33. Figure 1 reports
0.807 [90% CI 0.74, 0.88], which is compatible only with the factor reading,
so that is the form the model uses.

```{r ada-form}
ev_ada <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typ_events(800, id = 1, n_cyc = 5),
  typ_events(800, id = 2, n_cyc = 5, ada_from = 504)
)
auc_c5_typ <- function(mod) {
  s <- solve_typ(mod, ev_ada) |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc))
  r <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(dplyr::select(s, id, time, Cc), Cc ~ time | id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(ev_ada |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt), amt ~ time | id),
    intervals = data.frame(start = 2016, end = 2520, auclast = TRUE)
  ))
  a <- as.data.frame(r)
  a$PPORRES[a$id == 2] / a$PPORRES[a$id == 1]
}
ratio_factor <- auc_c5_typ(mod_typ)
ratio_exp <- auc_c5_typ(mod_typ |> rxode2::ini(e_ada_pos_cl = exp(1.11)))
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Reading = c("CL x 1.11 (used)", "CL x exp(1.11)", "Figure 1"),
    `AUC ratio` = c(ratio_factor, ratio_exp, 0.807), check.names = FALSE
  ),
  digits = 3, caption = "Typical ADA-positive / ADA-negative steady-state AUC ratio."
)
stopifnot(
  abs(ratio_factor - 1 / 1.11) < 0.02,
  ratio_exp < 0.5
)
```

# Exposure-response: objective response rate (Figure 3)

The ORR model is linear on the logit in the average AUC per 21-day interval:
logit(p) = -2.48928 + 4.36e-8 * (AUC - AUCc). Table S7 labels the exposure
term 'centred' but does not print AUCc. The maintainers digitised the fitted
line of Figure 3 and solved for AUCc with the printed slope and intercept,
obtaining 1.54e7 ng*h/mL; an unconstrained fit of the digitised curve gives
a slope of 4.373e-8, within 0.3% of the printed value, which confirms the
reading. 1.54e7 sits between the 200 mg and 700 mg exposure ranges, as the
median of the 80-patient cohort would.

For an exposure-driven logistic model with an intercept, the fitted
probabilities in the analysis set sum to the observed number of responders
(9 of 80). A virtual gastric cohort of 40 patients per arm is simulated
(covariates as above; ADA incidence 32.7% at 200 mg and 17.4% at 700 mg,
Table S3), its average AUC over four cycles is computed with PKNCA, and the
ORR model is applied to it.

```{r orr-cohort}
ev_gc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_cohort(40, 200, 0.327, n_cyc = 4, id_offset = 1000L, treatment = "200 mg"),
  make_cohort(40, 700, 0.174, n_cyc = 4, id_offset = 2000L, treatment = "700 mg")
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_gc[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
sim_gc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, ev_gc, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")

nca_gc <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    sim_gc |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment),
    Cc ~ time | treatment + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
    ev_gc |> dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |> dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment),
    amt ~ time | treatment + id
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(start = c(0, 504, 1008, 1512), end = c(504, 1008, 1512, 2016), auclast = TRUE)
))
auc_avg <- as.data.frame(nca_gc) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(AUC_FAVEZELIMAB = mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

mod_orr <- readModelDb("Gaurav_2026_favezelimab_orr")
orr <- solve_typ(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod_orr, which = "sigma"),
  auc_avg |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 0L),
  keep = "treatment"
)

orr_tab <- orr |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_auc = median(AUC_FAVEZELIMAB),
    predicted = mean(prob_orr),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(observed = c(3 / 40, 6 / 40))
orr_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = treatment, "Median AUCavg (ng*h/mL)" = median_auc,
    "Mean predicted ORR" = predicted, "Observed ORR (Table S6)" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Simulated ORR by arm versus Table S6.")

overall_pred <- mean(orr$prob_orr)
round(overall_pred, 3)
# Score-equation check of the digitised centring: the mean fitted probability
# over the analysis set equals 9/80 = 0.1125. A centring of 0 instead would
# give about 0.29 here; the window allows for the virtual cohort's AUCs.
stopifnot(abs(overall_pred - 9 / 80) < 0.04)
```

The mean predicted ORR over both arms lands close to the observed 11.3%, which
is what the digitised centring has to deliver. Per arm, the model spreads the
two arms further apart than the raw 7.5% and 15.0%, because a single line
through 80 patients with 9 responders is not constrained to hit each arm. The
simulated median exposures (about 0.85e7 and 3.5e7 ng*h/mL) are also around
10% above the boxplot medians of Figure 3 (about 0.8e7 and 3.1e7), since the
virtual cohort uses the whole PK population's covariates rather than those of
gastric cancer patients.

```{r figure-3}
curve <- data.frame(AUC_FAVEZELIMAB = seq(0.5e7, 7.1e7, length.out = 100), time = 0, evid = 0L)
curve_sim <- solve_typ(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_orr, which = "sigma"), curve)
ggplot(curve_sim, aes(AUC_FAVEZELIMAB, prob_orr)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  geom_rug(data = orr, aes(x = AUC_FAVEZELIMAB, colour = treatment), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Favezelimab average AUC (ng*h/mL)", y = "Probability of objective response",
    colour = "Simulated arm",
    caption = "Replicates the fitted line of Figure 3 of Gaurav 2026; rug: simulated gastric cohort."
  )
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **ADA functional form.** Table 1 lists 'ADA Effect on CL' = 1.11 without its
  equation, and the Table 1 footnote equation omits it. The maintainers
  encode it as a multiplicative factor on linear CL (`CL * 1.11^ADA_POS`),
  because the exponential reading would cut the steady-state AUC of
  ADA-positive patients to about one third, against the 0.807 GMR in Figure 1
  (see the ADA form check above). ADA status is time-varying; the source
  carried the last observed status forward. It acts on linear CL only, not
  on Vmax.
* **Km unit.** The Methods give Km in ug/mL; Table 1 and the Results give
  ug/L. ug/L (= ng/mL) is used: it is the only reading under which the
  Michaelis-Menten arm produces the dose nonlinearity the paper reports and
  the statement that 800 mg troughs are 'much higher than Km'.
* **Albumin unit.** The Table 1 footnote and Table S2 label albumin 'g/dL',
  but the values (median 40, range 21-70.6), the Results ('<= 37 g/L') and
  Figure 1 are in g/L. The model takes `ALB` in g/L with reference 40 g/L.
* **Sex reference category.** The Methods say the most frequent category is
  the reference, which would be male, but the footnote equations apply the
  sex coefficients to males and the typical male CL in the Results equals
  0.0195 * exp(0.200). The equations are followed: female is the reference,
  and the model applies `exp(e_male_cl * (1 - SEXF))`.
* **Full covariate model.** All covariates are kept, including those whose
  95% CI includes zero (age, hepatic impairment, ECOG and renal impairment on
  Vc, albumin on Vc), because the source used a full-model approach that
  retains every prespecified covariate in the final model. The footnote
  equation shows only the effects whose CI excludes zero.
* **Reference values.** Weight is normalised to 71 kg (footnote equation),
  albumin to 40 g/L and age to 59 years (Table S2 medians), as the power
  model in the footnote centres on the median.
* **Residual error.** Monolix combined error; the paper does not say whether
  it is Monolix's `combined1` (SD = a + b * f, the Monolix default) or
  `combined2`. `combined1` is used.
* **Infusion duration** is not reported; the simulations assume 30 minutes.
  It does not affect AUC and has negligible effect on Cmax.
* **ORR centring value** (`auc_favezelimab_ref` = 1.54e7 ng*h/mL) was
  digitised by the maintainers from the fitted line of Figure 3 (about 470
  pixel columns; interquartile range of the per-column solutions
  1.525e7-1.555e7); no printed value exists. It is fixed in the model.
* **Average AUC definition.** 'AUCavg considering individual-specific dosing
  history' is taken as the mean AUC per 21-day interval over the treatment
  period. Because favezelimab reaches steady state within one or two cycles
  at these doses, the average is close to the steady-state dose / CL.
* **Virtual cohorts** draw covariates independently from the Table S2
  marginals; the source cohorts have correlated covariates (Tables S4-S5),
  which is why the simulated subgroup GMRs differ from Figure 1 for sex and
  race.
* **Safety endpoints.** Grade >= 3 drug-related AEs and drug-related AEOSI
  showed no significant exposure-response relationship, and the paper did no
  further modelling; no parameters exist to package.
* No erratum or correction notice was found on Europe PMC as of 2026-11-13.
